source_text:
Ὅσα οὖν παρεπέσαμεν καὶ ἐποιήσαμεν δια τινας παρεμπτώσεις τοῦ ἀντικειμένου, ἀξιώσωμεν ἀφεθῆναι ἡμῖν. καὶ ἐκεῖνοι δέ, οἵτινες ἀρχηγοὶ στάσεως καὶ διχοστασίας ἐγενήθησαν, ὀφείλουσιν τὸ κοινὸν τῆς ἐλπίδος σκοπεῖν.
οἱ γὰρ μετὰ φόβου καὶ ἀγάπης πολιτευόμενοι ἑαυτοὺς θέλουσιν μᾶλλον αἰκίαις περιπίπτειν ἢ τοὺς πλησίον: μᾶλλον δὲ ἑαυτῶν κατάγνωσιν φέρουσιν ἢ τῆς παραδεδομένης ἡμῖν καλῶς καὶ δικαίως ὁμοφωνίας,
καλὸν γὰρ ἀνθρώπῳ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι περὶ τῶν παραπτωμάτων ἢ σκληρῦναι τὴν καρδίαν αὐτοῦ, καθὼς ἐσκληρύνθη ἡ καρδία τῶν στασιαζόντων πρὸς τὸν θεράποντα τοῦ θεοῦ Μωϋσῆν, ὧν τὸ κρίμα πρόδηλον ἐγενήθη,
κατέβησαν γὰρ εἰς ᾅδου ζῶντες, καὶ θάνατος ποιμανεῖ αὐτούς.
Φαραὼ καὶ ἡ στρατιὰ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάντες οἱ ἡγούμενοι Αἰγύπτου, τά τε ἅρματα καὶ οἱ ἀνάβαται αὐτῶν οὐ δἰ ἄλλην τινὰ αἰτίαν ἐβυθίσθησαν εἰς θάλασσαν ἐρυθρὰν καὶ ἀπώλοντο, ἀλλὰ διὰ τὸ σκληρυνθῆναι αὐτῶν τὰς ἀσυνέτους καρδίας μετὰ τὸ γενέσθαι τὰ σημεῖα καὶ τὰ τέρατα ἐν γῇ Αἰγύπτου διὰ τοῦ θεράποντος τοῦ θεοῦ Μωῦσέως.
thought_title: Confession versus hardening, with the examples of Korah and Pharaoh
orientation: The author, writing from the church in Rome to the Corinthians, has just spoken of the blessing of forgiven sins and now turns to the need for confession and the fate of those who harden their hearts in faction.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore, as many things as we fell aside in and did through certain intrusions of the adversary, let us ask that they be forgiven us. And those also, whoever became leaders of faction and division, ought to consider the common thing of hope. For those who conduct themselves with fear and love wish themselves rather to fall into mistreatments than their neighbors; rather they bear condemnation of themselves than of the harmony handed down to us well and justly. For it is good for a person to confess concerning transgressions than to harden his heart, just as the heart of those who made faction against the servant of God Moses was hardened, whose judgment became evident. For they went down into Hades alive, and death will shepherd them. Pharaoh and his army and all the leaders of Egypt, the chariots and their riders, not through any other cause were sunk into the Red Sea and perished, but through the hardening of their foolish hearts after the signs and wonders happened in the land of Egypt through the servant of God Moses.

choices.why: The verb means to fall beside or slip aside; the literal sense keeps the spatial metaphor of deviation rather than a general 'transgressed'.
The noun means something inserted or intruding; 'intrusions' preserves the sense of external interference by the adversary.
The glossary requires 'faction' for στάσις; 'leaders' keeps the literal sense of ἀρχηγοί as those who began or led the movement.
The phrase is awkward in Greek; the literal rendering preserves the genitive construction and the sense of what is shared in hope.
περιπίπτειν means to fall around or into; 'mistreatments' renders αἰκίαι literally as acts of ill-treatment.
The verb ποιμαίνω means to shepherd or tend as a shepherd; the literal rendering preserves the striking image of death as shepherd.

bible_refs.note: κατέβησαν γὰρ εἰς ᾅδου ζῶντες (they went down into Hades alive) alludes to the fate of Korah and his company
θάνατος ποιμανεῖ αὐτούς (death will shepherd them) echoes Psalm 49:14 LXX (Psalm 49:14 English)
ἐβυθίσθησαν εἰς θάλασσαν ἐρυθρὰν καὶ ἀπώλοντο (they were sunk into the Red Sea and perished) alludes to the drowning of Pharaoh's army

pass_b_english: So then, for whatever we fell aside in and did because of certain intrusions of the adversary, let us ask that it be forgiven us. And those who became leaders of faction and division also owe it to consider the common hope.

For those who conduct themselves with fear and love would rather fall into mistreatments themselves than have their neighbors do so. Rather, they bring condemnation on themselves than on the harmony that was handed down to us so well and justly.

For it is good for a person to confess his transgressions rather than to harden his heart, just as the heart of those who made faction against Moses, the servant of God, was hardened. Their judgment became clear:
for they went down into Hades alive, and death will shepherd them.

Pharaoh and his army and all the leaders of Egypt, their chariots and their riders, were sunk into the Red Sea and perished for no other reason than this: their foolish hearts were hardened after the signs and wonders had happened in the land of Egypt through Moses, the servant of God.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening sentence by replacing the vague 'common thing of hope' with 'the common hope,' and smoothed the second paragraph's contrast so the subject of 'bring condemnation on themselves' is clearly the same people who would rather suffer mistreatment themselves.

last_rejected.why: 'thing' is not in glossary; 'common hope' or 'common good of hope' is clearer.
last_rejected.ruling: τὸ κοινὸν τῆς ἐλπίδος means ‘the common hope’/‘common good of hope’; ‘thing’ is unnecessary but does not alter meaning.

last_rejected.quote: let us ask that it be forgiven us.
last_rejected.why: Greek says ‘let us deem ourselves forgiven’, not that we request forgiveness.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀξιώω commonly means 'request/ask'; rendering 'let us ask that it be forgiven' is within normal range, not a meaning change.
